subject: Service commitments: clarifying uptime buckets, blackout exceptions, and response routing
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@terraedge.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@terraedge.com>, procurement@terraedge.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood MSA/Order Form — a few service-term clarifications

Hi Laura,

Thanks for sending the revised order form and MSA. Our legal and platform teams reviewed the SLA section and came back with three items they need clarified before procurement can proceed:

1) Uptime buckets — they asked us to confirm how partial-region outages are measured. Specifically: do you compute availability per-region or as a global weighted average?
2) Blackout windows — your draft lists scheduled maintenance will be notified 72 hours in advance; our ops team needs a guaranteed annual blackout cap (we proposed 72 hours/year) and an explicit carveout process for emergency security hotfixes.
3) Response routing & escalation — they want clarity on how P1/P2 routing behaves when Redwood Dedicated capacity is saturated and whether support will proactively open fallback requests to a secondary pool.

I've attached our internal support-matrix and annotated PDF of the redlines. Can you point us to who at Redwood will own the technical measurement definition (per-region vs global), and whether you can accept the 72-hour annual cap as a concession?

Looking forward to your response — we are trying to get this through the week.

Best,
Olivia
Head of Platform Ops
TerraEdge

Attachments: TerraEdge_SupportMatrix_v1.xlsx (Excel sheet), requested_redlines.pdf (annotated)
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@terraedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA/Order Form — a few service-term clarifications

Olivia — thanks for the clear notes and the matrix. Quick answers up front:

- Measurement: our platform calculates availability per-region by default and exposes both per-region and global weighted metrics. We can commit to the per-region SLA being the binding measurement in the order form if you need that for operational isolation.
- Blackout cap: we can discuss a 72-hour/year cap, but we need to align on exception carveouts (emergency security hotfixes and customer-requested migrations). We usually exclude emergency security patches (we have a defined emergency window) but are open to adding a formal carveout process.
- Response routing when Dedicated is saturated: default behavior is to queue and prioritize P1s to the next available capacity tier and trigger a routed failover to a compatible model variant. We can add an explicit clause that Redwood will notify TerraEdge and open a fallback escalation on your behalf if Dedicated saturation impacts P1s for >5 minutes.

I'll loop in Marissa (account lead) and Karthik (legal/product policy) to propose language. We reviewed your annotated PDF — attached is our suggested redline PDF and a short support-policy excerpt for the measurement definition.

Next step: Marissa will propose firm wording for the three bullets; Karthik will confirm whether the 72-hour cap needs extra guardrails.

— Laura
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW-7891_SLA_redlines_20261121.pdf (redline suggestions)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: internal: proposed clause language for TerraEdge — please review

Team — drafting proposed order-form language below; paste into the tracked PDF if this looks good. Short form language to present to TerraEdge: 

1) Availability measurement: "Availability shall be measured per-region (per physical or cloud region) and reported as a percentage of successful user-facing tokens over the billing period. A global weighted-availability metric is available for reference but shall not be used to determine Service Credits unless explicitly agreed in a customer addendum."

2) Blackout cap & emergency carveouts: "Redwood will not schedule more than 72 hours of scheduled maintenance per rolling 12-month period that would cause service unavailability for a customer in a given region (\"Blackout Cap\"). Emergency security patches that are reasonably necessary to remediate active exploits are excluded from the Blackout Cap; Redwood will provide a post-deployment summary within 48 hours for each emergency patch and a root-cause note where applicable."

3) P1 escalation when Dedicated saturated: "If Redwood Dedicated capacity for a customer's pinned pool is saturated such that P1 incidents experience degraded response or throughput, Redwood will (i) notify the customer's designated technical contact within 5 minutes, (ii) attempt immediate routing to the next compatible capacity tier, and (iii) if automatic routing is insufficient, Redwood will proactively open a fallback escalation ticket with the customer's permission and coordinate until P1 is resolved."

Questions for legal: Do we want to bind 'emergency security patches' to a defined CVE/active exploit threshold? Connor — any operational/monitoring concerns with the 5-minute notify + immediate routing language?

-Marissa

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: internal: proposed clause language for TerraEdge — please review

Marissa — technically we can do per-region as the binding metric. A couple of operational flags: 

- For the Blackout Cap, we should add "scheduled maintenance that results in degraded performance (but not full unavailability) does not count against the 72-hour cap" — TerraEdge ops will ask about that distinction.
- The 5-minute notification for P1 is tight but fine for automated alerts; we should keep language that allows 'reasonable attempts' for manual confirmation before opening an escalation ticket to avoid duplicate tickets.
- For emergency security patches, tying to a CVE/actively exploited indicator makes legal comfortable; propose: "Emergency security patches (actively exploited or otherwise high-risk CVEs identified by Redwood or a recognized security authority) are excluded."

I'll update the tracked redline PDF with these two clarifications.

-Connor

From: Tom Keller <tom.keller@terraedge.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@terraedge.com>, procurement@terraedge.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service commitments: clarifying uptime buckets, blackout exceptions, and response routing

Laura — thanks for the rapid follow-up and the proposed language. Two follow-ups from our side before we pass this to legal: 

1) Can you confirm the exact metric name and the telemetry endpoint we'll get for per-region availability (so our monitoring can pull the same signal)?
2) On blackout accounting: TerraEdge would like scheduled maintenance that causes partial degradation (e.g., increased latency) to count against the 72-hour cap if it materially affects customer-facing SLAs. We can accept a carveout for critical security exploits as suggested, but need the threshold defined.

We attached the annotated support matrix with inline comments on the P1/P2 routing examples. If you can add the telemetry endpoint and explicit CVE/authority threshold, we can circulate to legal this afternoon.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Procurement
TerraEdge

Attachments: TerraEdge_SupportMatrix_v1.xlsx (annotated)
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@terraedge.com>, Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@terraedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service commitments: clarifying uptime buckets, blackout exceptions, and response routing

Tom/Olivia — good points. Quick confirmations: 

- Telemetry endpoint: Redwood will publish a per-region availability feed at https://status.redwood.ai/feeds/availability/{customer-id}/{region} (read-only, tokenized). We'll provide TerraEdge a read token and a schema doc by EOD Wednesday.
- Blackout accounting: we'll count scheduled maintenance that materially degrades customer-facing SLA (e.g., latency increases leading to error-rate or request-timeout thresholds crossing your defined SLO) against the 72-hour cap. We'll add wording that materiality is determined by crossing the customer's configured SLO thresholds and call out the CVE threshold for emergency carveouts as "actively exploited CVEs as listed by a recognized authority (e.g., CISA KEV, NVD with active exploit reports) or Redwood-detected active exploitation."

Attached is a final tracked-redline that incorporates Connor's and Marissa's suggestions and the telemetry endpoint. If this looks good, we'll ask legal to accept these limited redlines and then circulate a final order-form for signature.

Thanks for the quick turn — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW-7891_SLA_redlines_20261124.pdf (final tracked-redline)
